column2: A fish mark shaped like a scorpion is ascribed to his feet, and a fish shaped like a dog is declared on his face.
On the hand there are many lines, and hair is remembered in the nostrils; the thumb is very long, and the little finger very long too.
Such bad marks exist in Kali in many ways; many good marks are in me, O lord of birds.
Vishnu's thirty-two marks are so only in comparison with Brahma and the others; this was told to you by Brahma with that intention in mind, O Lord.
There is no contradiction between what Brahma said and what I have said, O good one; the conch-necked one is shown as the expansion of what I said.
I counted the red lower lip and the red palate as one; so there is no contradiction, as is understood through knowledge.
The women beginning with Lakshmana are endowed with twenty-seven marks.
In the private parts, eyes, hands, breasts and belly, she has five marks fewer than Bharati;
her marks are neither like Rudra's nor others', O lord of birds. Varuni is endowed with twenty-six marks and lacks six;
in the ears, belly, nose, braid of hair, ankles and private parts there is some excess. Indra is endowed with twenty-five, O lord of birds, always lacking seven marks;
in the hands, feet, belly, ears, penis, ankles and lower lip there is excess. Nasatya-Vayu is endowed with twenty-four marks and lacks eight;
at the navel, ankles, jaw, feet, shoulders, teeth, eyes and lower lip there is excess. Shachi is endowed with twenty-three marks and has nine faults;
in the private parts, hair, lower lip, ears, shanks, cheeks, chest and ankles, and the upper lip, there is some excess; so understand, best lord of birds.
The wind called Pravaha has twenty-two marks and ten faults, with some excess in the thumb; the sun has twenty marks and eleven faults.
One is endowed with twenty marks and has twelve faults; Agni is endowed with nineteen marks and has thirteen deficiencies.
Vaivasvata has eighteen marks and fourteen deficiencies; Mitra, O bird, has seventeen marks
and fifteen faults; there is no doubt. The lord of wealth has sixteen of them, without doubt,
and is declared to have sixteen deficiencies. Agni's eldest son has fifteen of them
and seventeen faults, without doubt. The Ganga is declared to have fourteen of them
and eighteen faults, without doubt. Budha has thirteen of them
and nineteen faults, without doubt. Shani has twenty faults and twelve marks.
Pushkara is declared to have eleven marks and twenty-one defects.
The long-lived ancestors, O bird, have ten marks and twenty-three faults, without doubt.
The best of the divine Gandharvas have eight marks and are declared to have twenty-four faults.
The human Gandharvas have seven marks and are declared to have twenty-five faults.
The kings of the earth have six good qualities and twenty-six faults; others have five, and some only four;
some have three; lower than that there are none, O best of birds. In whatever man or king, O lord of birds, an excess of marks is seen,
they are neither true men nor true kings, nor all always the highest. All gods and Daityas, O lord of birds,
have been described in order by their marks and lack of marks; there is no doubt. Those endowed with twenty-seven marks, O bird,
are therefore to be known as well-marked, not those with thirty-two marks. Growing up in her father's house, always seeking to make her family excellent, O lord of birds,
she said to her father, as food and the like were being given to friends and others: "Those who always give with awareness of him dwelling within, present here and there —
the good say that food and drink given without that knowledge are given in vain. I will tell of Hari dwelling here and there; hear it attentively today and always.
Hari as a child, Krishna in the form of a child, takes milk, fresh butter and ghee, and always ornaments and clothes; so one should always give for Vishnu's satisfaction.
Hari called Keshava, Mukunda, enjoys through friends the food and drink given; a householder should always give first and be blessed; otherwise it is in vain.
Hari called Madhava always receives it — knowing this, one should give food and the like; Vishnu is always pleased by what is given with this knowledge, otherwise it is in vain.
In the house Vasudeva, Hari, always dwells and is always pleased, O Suparna; knowing this, one should always adorn one's house with metal images.
The one called Govinda dwells among Vaishnavas, Vasudeva dwells with the sons; Mukunda in a friend, Aniruddha in a brother-in-law, and Narayana always in the best of brahmins.
In the cowshed Hari always dwells in Vishnu's form; in the horse always dwells the one called Vamana; Sankarshana always dwells in the shudra class, and Pradyumna always in the vaishya;
Janardana always dwells in the kshatriya class, and Hari as Mahidasa always among fishermen; the one Hari called Upendra always dwells in the earth, O Suparna.
The discus-bearer always dwells in the elephant; Vishvarupa always dwells within; the sustainer of beings always dwells in the dog, and in the ant too, always.
Trivikrama dwells in the sky in Hari's form, and Hari in endless forms in all species. Hari has no class, no lineage, no caste — the Lord of all forms, wondrous."
Knowing this, the goddess Lakshmana always pleased Hari with the worship she performed, thinking, 'Hari is my husband.'
Longing to have Vishnu as her husband she gave up her body, and was born a daughter among the Madras, O lord of birds. At Lakshmana's svayamvara I pierced the target and put the kings to flight,
took Lakshmana's hand, went to the city and delighted the goddess. Likewise I will tell you of my marriage to Jambavati and the reason for her becoming my wife.

When shall I see Shrinivasa's chest, broad and adorned with the Shrivatsa and jewels? When shall I see Shrinivasa's belly, beautiful and marked with three folds?
garudpurana:311:35	When shall I see Shrinivasa's throat, like a conch, support of Maharloka? When shall I see Shrinivasa's navel, full, always the support of the sky?
garudpurana:311:36	When shall I see Murari's face, always the support of Janaloka?
garudpurana:311:37	When shall I see Shrinivasa's head, always the support of Satyaloka? When shall I see Shrinivasa's waist, always the support of Bhurloka?
garudpurana:311:38	When shall I see Shrinivasa's thighs, always the support of Talatala? When shall I see Shrinivasa's knees, most tender, the support of Sutala?
garudpurana:311:39	When shall I see Shrinivasa's shanks, always the support of Rasatala? When shall I see the soles of Hari's feet, always the support of Patala?
Reflecting thus on the way, the goddess saw on Sheshachala the god Shesha, shining with a thousand hoods, with various trees, and with monkeys male and female.
Through merit gathered over endless births I have seen today this supreme mountain. At the sight of it, her eyes filled with tears, she rose at once and bowed with her head.
One should bow on seeing its face, not at its back or other parts. She bowed twelve times, placing a shalagrama before it.
So should Vaishnavas do toward the mountain; others do the opposite. Within Madhva, on the mountain's summit, Shrinivasa dwells always, worshipped by Rama, Brahma and the others.
I will see the supreme, most excellent Shrinivasa; now I wish to climb the mountain. Having said this, she made her stay at the tirtha called Kapila together with her father.
Here Shrinivasa, Hari, dwells in material form, and not otherwise. First bathing and having her head shaved there, and having the tirtha shraddha performed at the holy tirtha,
and giving every gift — cows, land, gold and the rest — the virtuous woman climbed the mountain; placing the shalagrama before her, she bowed again with great devotion.
Climbing thus up to a hundred steps, she sat down there and heard the Bhagavata Purana, and heard the praise of Venkatadri.
From Jaigishavya, her revered teacher, with great devotion, she heard the whole truth of Venkatadri.
Having bathed properly at that tirtha and given a lamp to an excellent brahmin, they went again to see Shrinivasa, saying, "Govinda, Govinda."
Reaching the place presided over by the chief Prana, she sat down there and said: "Jaigishavya, how should the darshan of Shrinivasa, Vishnu, be made? Tell me that."
Jaigishavya, delighted at heart, said: "I will tell you the method; listen, maiden. Having heard it from me, do all I say. Seeing the first gate of Shrinivasa, say:
'Thousands of offences are committed by me day and night; forgive them all, O God, Supreme Person.
Faults of mind, speech and body of every kind, and whatever causes hatred of Vaishnavas in me — reduce them to ashes, O Madhava.'
At the first gate of Shrinivasa, goddess, one should duly remember Vijaya and Jaya; at the southern side of Shrinivasa, goddess, one should duly remember Chanda and Prachanda;
at the western side of Shrinivasa, goddess, one should remember with devotion Nanda and Sunanda; at the left gate of Shrinivasa, maiden, one should remember Kumudaksha and Kumuda.
Whoever enters with devotion, thinking, 'When shall I see him?' with reverence, goddess, should circumambulate twelve times and remember Shrinivasa at every step.
Having sipped water properly at Shri Swami tirtha, bowed, bathed and bowed to Bhuvaraha, goddess, one should enter the inner gate with devotion, saying, 'Govinda, Govinda.'
Then one should make a full prostration to Hari and enter the temple; entering again through the gate, standing there, one should meditate in mind on the gods seated on the pedestal.
In the middle of the pedestal, goddess, one should bow to Shrinivasa, Narayana, the full one; to the left of the god, outside the pedestal, one should bow to the Guru-deva.
In front of the pedestal and below it, in the south-east corner, one should bow [to Ganesha]; in the south-west, goddess, the Vaishnava should always bow to Vyasadeva.
In the north-west corner one should bow with devotion to Durga, one's self grown in devotion. Above the pedestal, in the south-east, goddess, salutations to Yama, presiding over dharma;
above the pedestal, in the upper south-west corner, one should bow to Vayu, lord of knowledge; above the pedestal in the north-west, fair-browed one, to Rudra, lord of detachment;
above the pedestal in the north-east, goddess, to the god Indra, lord of powers; to the east of the pedestal one should bow to Nirriti, lord of the Aryaman, here, goddess;
to the south of the god's pedestal one should bow to Durga called Ugrarupa; to the west of the pedestal, maiden, one should bow to Kamadeva, lord of health;

to the north of the god's pedestal one should remember the god Rudra, lord of the absence of powers; in the middle of the pedestal one should always bow to Varaha, maiden, the supreme one called Purusha.
Above him one should always bow to Lakshmi called Shakti, in the form of the support; above that one should bow to Vayu and the tortoise, and above that to Shesha and the tortoise;
above that the fair-browed one should bow to the goddess of the earth who presides over it; above that one should remember Varuna, lord of the ocean of milk.
Above that one should bow to Lakshmi, and worship the one called Shvetadvipa, maiden; above that one should bow to Lakshmi, the great divine one called the pavilion.
In the middle of the pedestal one should worship Lakshmi called Yama, the goddess in the midst of Yama; to the right of the god Yama one should bow to the Sun in the form of a lamp, good lady;
to the left of the god Yama one should bow to the goddess Shri in the form of a lamp; in front of the god Yama one should bow to Fire in the form of a lamp.

In front of the god one should bow to the one named Bhumi and always remember the deity presiding over the principles; one should bow to Durga, presiding over tamas, as the couch of Shrinivasa, Vishnu.
One should bow to the one Self in the form of the eastern steps of the pedestal, goddess, and to the one of knowledge in the form of the southern steps, maiden.
On the eastern petal of the lotus, goddess, to the one in female form called Vimala, and bow to the gods beginning with Brahma; on the south-east petal, listen,
one should bow to the supreme goddess named Utkarsha, and to Rama, Brahma, Vayu and Shesha; and on the eight petals of the southern lotus to the female forms of Narayana, Shesha and the others;
salutation is to be made to the female forms, maiden, by me, on the western petal, of Gopa-Narayana, Brahma, Vayu, the brahmins and others, Shesha, Rudra and others;
salutation is to be made to the female forms on the north-eastern petals, of Ishana-Narayana, Viranchi, Vayu, the sky, Shesha, the gods and others.
Likewise in the middle of the lotus, salutation is to be made to the goddess called Anugraha, Vishnu's Lakshmi, and to the female forms of Vayu, the sky, Shesha, Rudra and others.
One should always bow to the glorious one called Ananta, who is the very form of the yoga-pedestal, and so bow to the god Shrinivasa.
To the left of Shrinivasa the wise should bow to Lakshmi; to the right of Shrinivasa, auspicious one, one should bow to Dhara.
Outside the pedestal, on the east, one should bow to auspicious Kripolka; to Maholka on the south, and to Virolka on the west;
and on the north one should make salutation to the great-souled Dyulka; in all four corners the wise should bow to Sahasrolka.
On the east one should bow to Vasudeva; on the south to the god Sankarshana; on the west to Pradyumna;
on the north, untiring, one should bow to Aniruddha; in the south-east, maiden, one should always bow to Maya, auspicious one;
one should bow to Jaya in the south-west, and to Kriti in the north-west; in the north-east one should bow to the one called Shanti.
On the east salutation to Keshava and to Narayana; one should bow to Madhava in the south-west and the north-west;
in the south-east, maiden, always with devotion and self-restraint, auspicious one, one should bow to Govinda, and on the south to Vishnu;
one should bow to Madhusudana, maiden, in the south-west; on the west to Trivikrama and to Vamana;
one should bow to Vishnu Shridhara, passionate one; on the north, great maiden, salutation to Hrishikesha,
and likewise, untiring, one should bow to Padmanabha; and to Damodara in the north-east, passionate one.
In the fourth enclosure, on the east, salutation to the Great Tortoise; one should bow to Varaha in the south-east, auspicious maiden;
on the south salutations again and again to Narasimha and Vamana; one should bow to Bhargava in the south-west with a pure mind;
on the west salutation to Madhava and to Krishna; one should bow to Buddha in the north-west, auspicious maiden;
on the north, salutation to you, Ananta, in the form of a meteor; in the north-east, untiring, one should bow to Vishvarupa.
One should bow to Varuni in the south-east, Gayatri in the south-west, Bharati in the north-west and Girija in the north-east.
To the left of Girija one should bow to Sauparni. On the east one should bow to Indra with his weapons,
with his retinue — salutations again and again to Shri Vishnu's attendant. In the south-east to you, Agni, 'with his weapons,' as before;
on the south to Yama; in the south-west one should worship Nirriti; on the west to Varuna; in the north-west salutation to Vayu;
on the north to Kubera and in the north-east to Shiva; between Ishana and Shakra, to Brahma with his weapons;
and between Nirriti and [Varuna], salutations again and again to Shesha. Having made salutation thus, one should bow again and again.
This is the whole account of darshan according to rule; after this one should go for the darshan of Lakshmi's lord."
Having heard this, the goddess went joyfully with them. The rule of Shrinivasa's darshan that has been told, O bird, should never be told to anyone, because it is secret.
Meeting with the good who teach the true principles is hard to come by, O lord of birds; through merit gathered over many births she met her teacher.

Milk gives up its own change, the rest gives up the rest, the lotus its mud; through union with the lotus-naveled one the restless mind, and through the company of the good, inauspicious things do not arise.
Because he is lord of the lingas he is called Vyankatesha. Since the hosts of Daityas are devoid of knowledge and the like, the host of Daityas is called Vyankata;
as the Lord who destroys them, he is named Vyankata. Since qualities like desire and anger are opposed to bliss,
they are called Vyankatas, and the Lord destroys them; therefore he is called Vyankatesha. Knowing this, perform japa.
Having heard thus the greatness of Vyankata, O lord of birds, the goddess slept there that night with her father; rising in the Brahma muhurta, the maiden remembered in her heart:

(Morning hymn to Vyankatesha.) "Shri Vyankatesha and the form of Narasimha, Shri Varadaraja and the form of Varaha, the one who reclines at Shrirangam and the one who reclines on Ananta — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
The form of Shri Krishna and Gadadhara, Shri Vishnupada, the one who dwells at Prayaga, Narayana who dwells at Shri Badari — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
Damodara, abode of the three worlds, Shri Panduranga and the god Narasimha, the god Shri Rama and the one who dwells at Amogha — may all of them make my morning auspicious.

Shri Dharmaputra and the form of Narasimha, the one dwelling in the pippala tree and the one dwelling at Muhalla, Kola-Narasimha and the lion at Shurpakara — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
The four-faced one and lovely Sarasvati, Bharati, Sharva, Suparna and Shesha, Uma, great Indra and those led by Shachi — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
Dvaravati, Kashi and Avantika, Prayaga and Kanchi, the city of Mathura, Mayavati and the city of Hastimati — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
The Bhagirathi and Sarasvati, the Godavari, Sindhu, Krishna and Veni, Kalinda's daughter the Yamuna, and the Narmada — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
The Vitasta, Kaveri with the Tungabhadra, Suvanjara, Bhimarathi, Vipasha, the Tamraparni and the Pinakini — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
The Swami Pushkarini and the Suvarnamukhari, Shri Pandavi, Tumburu, Kapila and Papanashini —
the teacher Vasishtha, Kratu and Angiras, Manu, Pulastya, Pulaha and Gautama, Raibhya, Marichi, Chyavana and Daksha — may all of them make my morning auspicious.
The seven oceans and the seven principal mountains, the seven continents and seven groves, and the seven worlds beginning with Bhu — may all of them make my morning auspicious.

Mandhatri, Nahusha, Ambarisha and Sagara, King Nala, Dharmaraja, Prahlada, the king of sacrifices, Vibhishana and Gaya, Vyasa and Hanuman too, Ashvatthama, Kripa, Uma, Drupada's daughter, Shri Janaki, Tara, Mandodari — may all make my morning greatly auspicious always, O Hari.

The groves of ashvattha, and the groves of tulasi and amla, O Lord, the groves of punnaga and champaka and other flowers, the groves of mandara and Hari's fragrant ones — may they always grant me joy, O Lord Shri Venkatesha."

Remembering Shrinivasa thus, the goddess performed her purifications with Jaigishavya, went to Hari's Pushkarini to bathe and bathed properly there; having duly recited the mantra of Vyankatesha, she spoke to Jaigishavya, her teacher.
Bathing there and hearing of the form of Vamana, they say the fruit equals that of giving; the Chandratirtha is declared to measure ten cubits.
A bath there at midday is hard for men to obtain, most auspicious one; staying there, the blessed man always worships Hari.
The gift of a shalagrama with the form of Varaha is rare; it is the size of a jambu fruit, like a hen's egg,
its mouth ring-shaped and the size of a chickpea, on the left side of the stone, leaving aside the middle,
with two discs, and at the top, passionate one, marked with a golden dot — it is called Bhuvaraha.
Worshipping Bhuvaraha, giving the image and hearing of it, and seeing Bhuvaraha dwelling there, that man has done his duty in the world.
Whoever, having bathed there, hears properly the marks of the image of Bhuvaraha gains that merit, goddess, and shares in liberation; there is nothing to consider here.
In the north-east of Shrinivasa, goddess, is the Raudra tirtha, supreme and purifying; staying there, the great god Rudra always worships Shrinivasa.

They say it measures eight cubits; Vaishnavas should bathe there. Bathing there with self-restraint, one should hear with reverence the divine story of Murari; one should bathe, drink and give there, and Lakshmi-Narasimha is always pleased, goddess. [A stone] the size of a jujube fruit, round and marked with a dot,
with two discs on the left side of the deity, with golden lines and a little red,
of vaishya colour, with a mouth, marked with lotus lines and the like — know that to be Lakshmi-Narasimha, giver of enjoyment and liberation.
Know that the gift of such an image of Gandaki stone is hard to accomplish, O lord of birds. Bathing there, one should hear with devotion of the form of Shri Narasimha, Lakshmi's lord;
one gains the fruit of giving the image, goddess — truly, truly; there is nothing to consider.
Between Ishana and Shakra is the tirtha called Brahmatirtha; a bath there is rare for men and accomplishes every aim.
The gift of a shalagrama there is rare for men, and the gift of an image of Lakshmi-Narayana very rare.
Its size is declared equal to an udumbara fruit, umbrella-shaped, round, with a pleasing, auspicious face;
the mouth is declared to be the size of a chickpea; on the left and right sides evenly full,
coloured like a calf among a herd of cows, with four discs, marked with cow's hoof-prints and golden scars,
with a forest garland and feathered like thunderbolt-arrows — such an image of Hari they know as Lakshmi-Narayana.
In Kali, obtaining it is held to be rare for men on earth, and giving it rarer still, goddess; what shall I tell you?
Having bathed at Brahmatirtha, one should hear the story of Hari. Of the Gandaki stone of Lakshmi-Narayana,
whoever knows the marks then gains a like fruit, without doubt; there is no need to consider this.
To the east of Shrinivasa's tirtha is Indratirtha; Shachi's lord dwells there to worship Shrinivasa.
The gift of a shalagrama stone should be made to a learned Vedic brahmin; the gift of a shalagrama stone destroys a crore of killings.
Whoever, goddess, gives at that tirtha the stone called Sita-Rama becomes like a king on earth, good lady.
The Sita-Rama stone, goddess, is declared to be of two kinds: one with five discs, one with six.
Of these the one with six discs is declared best; its fruit is said to be double that of the one with five discs.
The size of a hen's egg, very glossy and blue, with three mouths, six discs and filaments,
with golden lines, and with banner, thunderbolt and goad — such a stone, good lady, is remembered as Sita-Rama.
Its cavity, goddess, in the mouth and face of Sita-Rama — it is rare for men in Kali, auspicious, and grants sovereignty over oneself.
At Indratirtha, great goddess, the stone called Sita-Rama — its gift is rare, the fruit of no small austerity.
If one is unable to give, one should hear Hari's marks; one then gains the fruit of giving a shalagrama stone.
In the south-east of Shrinivasa, goddess, is the excellent tirtha called Vahni; the fire-god always dwells in the midst of the tirtha to worship Shrinivasa.
Whoever bathes with devotion at the tirtha called Vahni, goddess, remembering the Unborn, attains liberation through knowledge, goddess; a bath there is rare for men.
Know that bathing at that king of tirthas is hard, and devotion to it rare, goddess; the gift of the shalagrama stone called Vasudeva is very rare:
short, round, blue, with a fine mouth, a pure disc at the mouth, and a fine bamboo-like line — this is called Vasudeva; its gift in Kali is rare, good lady.
If one cannot give it, goddess, having bathed at the tirtha one should properly hear the marks of the stone called Vasudeva; the great say the fruit of the two is equal.
To the south of Shrinivasa is remembered Yamatirtha; there King Yama always dwells to worship Hari.
Bathing and giving there are held to be supreme and imperishable; the gift of a shalagrama stone should be made there, great sage.
The gift of the stone called Pattabhirama is desired there; it is as large as a mango fruit, with three mouths,
without a disc on the head, with seven discs, blue, with golden lines and marked with cow's hooves and the like.
Pattavardhana-Rama is rare and gives much fortune; whoever gives Pattavardhana-Rama there becomes one consecrated to the throne; there is no need to consider this.
In the south-west of Shrinivasa is the excellent Nairrita tirtha; Nirriti always dwells there to worship.
One should bathe there; there is no rebirth. Of the shalagrama stone, the one called Purushottama —
the mortal who gives that image goes to the supreme goal. Shaped like an udumbara fruit, with a pleasing, auspicious face,
with two discs and a disc on the head, marked with a golden dot, with thunderbolt and goad —
the gift of that image is rare there, since the great-souled god Shrinivasa is pleased by it. When giving is hard, goddess, one should hear the marks of that image.
Between Pashi and Nairrita is the supreme Sheshatirtha; bathing there, whoever gives a Shesha image to a brahmin
goes to the supreme world from which there is no return. Shaped like an udumbara fruit and like an earring,
its mouth like Shesha, with two discs in it; the fruit with one disc and marked like an anthill,
of some colour — the Shesha image is very clear. The Shesha image is declared to be of two kinds, sleeping and awakened;
the awakened has raised hoods, with seven lakh hoods; of these the sleeping one is rare and remembered as bringing great fortune,
giving liberation in this world and the next; there is no doubt. Where there are from nine up to twenty discs,
it is to be known as Ananta, giver of endless fruit; above twenty, fair-faced one, it is to be known as Vishvambhara,
and even then with filaments, discs and marks. In Kali it is rare for men, and its gift very rare.
Having bathed at Sheshatirtha with a pure mind and heard these marks, one goes to the supreme goal.
After that, fortunate one, is the excellent Varuna tirtha; there the god Varuna always dwells to worship Hari.
One should bathe there and give an excellent gift; one desiring prosperity should give at this tirtha, fair one, the Shishumara, the Matsya or the Trivikrama stone.
The size of a jambu fruit, fine at the tail and marked with a dot, with three discs at the mouth and a disc above the tail,
rich with the Shrivatsa, dots and a garland — this is declared the Matsya image; with a disc below the tail it is declared the Shishumara;
if it has a crooked disc it is declared Trivikrama. Hearing their marks at the excellent Varuna tirtha,
one gains the fruit of giving them and rejoices in Vishnu's abode. In the house where the images described above dwell, passionate one, the Bhagirathi, best of tirthas, is present, without doubt.
A bath in the Swami Pushkarini is hard for men in Kali, and bathing in the tirthas there very hard;
the gift of a shalagrama stone is likewise held to be hard, and giving a daughter in marriage on the bank of the Swami Pushkarini very hard;
the gift of a tawny cow is hard, and a gift of food very hard, at the Swami Pushkarini tirtha and at the other tirthas, passionate one.
Bathe as prescribed, and likewise make the gift of a bed. Addressed thus by the sage Jaigishavya, the maiden,
firm in her vow, bathed in the Swami Pushkarini; having bathed well at these tirthas, the lovely one gave gifts.
The goddess stayed there three times seven days. Whoever hears the greatness of the bank of the Swami Pushkarini attains supreme devotion to Shrinivasa, who pervades the world.
She circumambulated the Lord of Venkata with her whole body in devotion, and pleased the brahmins and others with clothes, perfumes, ornaments and the like.
Again the next morning, having bathed in the water of the Swami Pushkarini, the fortunate one went to the one called Tumburu.
The goddess asked her teacher, "Master, what is this called?" Jaigishavya said: "This is known as Tumburu, fair lady.
Long ago Narada stood in austerity here with Tumburu; here Vishnu appeared for Narada's good.
Whoever bathes here goes to the supreme goal; a bath here is rare for all men in Kali.
A bath here for men is the fruit of no small austerity." Bathing and drinking there and giving gifts,
the goddess came back and bowed to Shrinivasa, and that day she satisfied the brahmins, passionate one.
Reaching the Swami Pushkarini, the virtuous one lit lamps; with rows of lamps on the steps the fortunate one readily pleased the Lord of gods, Shrinivasa, teacher of the world.
Again the next day she reached the unsurpassed Shakratirtha; that tirtha, above the one called Kapila, is remembered as purifying.
Bathing there, the fortunate one should herself bathe above it; there is the lake of Vishvaksena, which destroys all sins.
Above that the fortunate one went and saw the tirthas of the five weapons, and bathed in them.
Above that is the Agnikunda, hard to climb, and beyond it; above it is Brahmatirtha, which frees one from brahmin-slaying.
Above that is the holy tirtha of the seven sages, of good fruit; the fruit of those tirthas increases tenfold, each higher than the last.
Who here is able to describe their greatness? At the tirthas of the sages that maiden performed excellent austerity.
Performing excellent austerity until my incarnation, she gave up her body by yogic concentration and in the house of Jambavan
was born as Jambavati and grew up in his home. Her father Jambavan then gave me the maiden; after Rukmini she is my wife, O lord of birds.
This is the supreme narrative of the great mountain Venkatadri; what man on earth other than me is able to describe it?
Lakshmi always prepares the food-offering of Venkatesha, and Brahma always worships him; this is the conclusion of scripture.
One should not mock men who eat the food-offering; even if one thinks oneself not excellent, the food-offering, jaggery and the like, should be taken, without doubt; otherwise one goes to hell.
There has never been and will never be a god higher than Shrinivasa. Cooking yourself food made with ghee and the like, offer it to Shrinivasa and then eat.
This supreme secret I have told you, O lord of birds; it should not be told to anyone, since it is secret, best of birds. Now I will tell of the gradation; hear, O Lord.
The habit of relishing flavours in eating food not offered to Vishnu, the same habit with offerings, the same habit in eating what is forbidden,
the same habit in licking what should not be licked and drinking what should not be drunk — abandoning the true nature of the two, the fool accepts them again and again, always.
They say his bathing is useless; therefore it should be given up; neither of the two should be done. Understand this intention, O lord of birds, always with a smile.

Without knowing the nature of his two wives, accepting one and abandoning the other, the dull-witted one bathes and so on; they say it is useless — neither liberation nor enjoyment comes. If all this is false, then let the king of serpents bite me.
Garuda said: "Tell me what the two wives are, and what their nature is, O Murari; tell me which of the two is the wife to be accepted, and tell me properly which is not to be accepted."

Shri Krishna said: "The intellect is the wife, and she has two forms, O lord of birds: one wicked and the other of good form. Of the two, the wicked one is the younger; the elder is of the nature of good understanding.
Through the younger the soul goes to ruin; through the one who stands well, it reaches fitting standing. Hear, I will tell you the nature of the younger; having heard it, resolve to abandon her.
The younger, impelling the soul, always practises dharma for desired ends: 'Where are brahmins, where is the great Vishnu, where are stories, where sacrifices, where cows,
where the ashvattha, where bathing, where purity? All this brings ruin.' To her foolish husband: 'Worship Renuka; give lamps to the goddess Maya;
worship Subhairava and the others, you blind fool; always wear turmeric powder. On Jyeshtha Ashtami worship the goddess Jyeshtha, and tie a thread around your neck with devotion.
On Marigandha Ashtami worship Marigandha and likewise wear a thread on your neck. On an auspicious day worship the lamp-post and wear its thread on your neck.
Worship Mahalakshmi and Adyalakshmi properly with devotion, O soul; wear Lakshmi's thread on your neck, and hereafter you will be rich in great fortune.

Setting aside the day of the sacred thread, desiring fortune, wear fine guggulu with great devotion; quickly worship married women with devotion, pleasing them with perfumes, flowers, incense and lamps;
placing a fine arati in a bronze plate, wave it before gods and non-gods; spreading neem leaves on the ground, bow, saying, "Forgive me."
Worship Mahadevi today with devotion, and do not give food to good Vaishnavas; if you give food to good Vaishnavas, your fortune will perish before your eyes.
Holding a bamboo vessel in your left hand and a lamp in your right, husband, rise and beg alms at five houses, casting away all shame.
First, at home, prepare food of six flavours and eat a meal hidden from the world; feeding the leftover food, husband, take refuge in them;
placing their hands on a book, make them say with their mouths, "Protect." Worship today the sword-god, husband, and worship his servants properly;
with them make the sound of dogs, and always apply turmeric powder. Perform the worship of Bhimasena with the five nectars and the sixteen offerings;
have a silver loincloth made for him and offer it, and light a row of lamps; feed his best servants today with devotion, and roar well, "Bhima, Bhima!"
Delight his best servants always with your own clothes, with liquor and heaps of meat. Worship Mahadeva today properly with the Maharudra and Atirudra;
saying "Hara," worship the Jangamas, shudras skilled in the Shaiva Agamas. On Shakambhari's day, cooking all vegetables well, from house to house
give them with devotion and great reverence, adorning yourself and praising her virtues. Worship the family god today with devotion, with your eyes on that day, thinking him to be Shambhu;
worship his best devotees properly today and bow at their feet. On the fifth day worship an earthen Shesha image with milk, parched rice and the like;
tying a fine snake-noose around your neck, eat again of its leftover food. On the fourth day eat with devotion; eat the food-offering well today.'
Impelling her husband with such things, she always makes the soul perish. Through association with her, the husband who is the soul is well bitten here and hereafter.
Cast off association with her far away and always act fully [on the good]. The one who has the form of good understanding, urging him, said: 'Worship Vishnu with great reverence;
always worship no one but Hari; that Renuka will not protect you. If Hari, called the Unseen, were not always the giver of fruit, O lord of birds —
always serving the goddess despised and not mentioned in scripture, hostile to husbands, through her grace you would suffer leprosy, fistula and the like, and go to Samyamani.

Then, tell me, where would that evil goddess have gone? So, husband, do not worship that goddess. Husband, worship brahmins and Vaishnavas, of good form, who carry one across the sorrow of worldly existence.
Setting aside pure service and the like, what comes from worshipping the goddess Maya? Tell me. Having worshipped on Jyeshtha Ashtami the goddess Jyeshtha, who is Alakshmi, thinking her Lakshmi,
and tying her thread on your neck, you will experience many sorrows, husband. When, husband, bound with nooses by Yama's messengers and well beaten with whips,
where will that Alakshmi flee then? So worship the root, Vishnu's feet. Husband, always worship the principle of Vayu, and do not resort to Skanda, fool;
[offering] butter to him with devotion and eating his leftovers, husband, and tying his thread on your neck, you will experience sorrows here, husband.
When, husband, bound with nooses by Yama's messengers and well beaten with whips — where will Skanda flee then? So worship the root, Vishnu's feet.
Having had a lamp-post given and tied its thread on your neck with devotion, husband, when you are bound by Yama's messengers with nooses and well beaten with lamp-posts,
where will the lamp-post have fled? So worship the root, Vishnu's feet. Having worshipped Lakshmi on Lakshmi's day, you wear her thread on your neck;
when, husband, bound with nooses by Yama's messengers and well beaten with whips — where will that Lakshmi flee? So worship the root, Vishnu's feet.
On the day of marriage and the sacred thread, dull-minded one, wearing despised things with great devotion, placing the arati in a bronze plate and waving it with the sound 'Udaudai,'
and likewise, seeing neem leaves and dancing with great reverence — when you are bound and bound again with nooses by Yama's messengers and well beaten,
where has your family god, master, great soul, fled? Tell me. Having worshipped your own bodies properly, with throat-ornaments and the hair of widows,
when you stand there and the mighty messengers of Yama beat you with pestles and javelins, where has she fled, hairless and long-eared?
The fool who, holding a bamboo vessel in his left hand and a lamp in his right, goes begging from house to house, while the goddess stays in his house —
when he is burned well with thousands of lamps by Yama's messengers, fool, where has noseless Renuka fled, dull-minded one? Tell me.
Always, fool, worshipping the sword-god with devotion, properly, like a devotee, and roaring like a dog with them while staying in your own house always —
when you are well beaten by Yama's messengers, crying out there, where did that god flee then, abandoning his best devotee who stood there?
The fool who, separately, worships an image of Bhimasena properly with the five nectars, and gives fine sauces, food and a loincloth, staying in his own house —
when the fool is well beaten by Yama's messengers on Yama's road, where has that Bhima fled? So worship the root, Vishnu's feet.
Having worshipped Mahadeva properly and said "Hara" while living in your house — when the house is burned by fire, where has Hara fled then?
On Shakambhari's day, everything — where has that goddess Shakambhari fled, great soul? Tell me. Having worshipped the potter's god with devotion,
when on the fifth day you have worshipped with devotion an earthen Shesha image while living in your house, and then Yama's messengers bind you well and fasten you with snake-nooses,
where has the Naga fled, abandoning his best devotee? Tell me. Having worshipped Vinayaka with durva sprouts, modakas and the five foods,
when you stand there and are well beaten by Yama's messengers with heated rods, fool, where has the king of obstacles fled, leaving behind his tusk? Tell me.
The fool who, at the time of marriage, has worshipped the flour-goddess with great devotion while living in his own house — when he is bound and tormented by Yama's messengers on Yama's road,
where has the dung-goddess fled, abandoning her tormented devotee? The fool who at the time of marriage goes to the washerman's house and entreats him properly,
winds the post-thread around the pitcher, worships it and lives in his own house — when Yama's messenger places that post-thread in his mouth
and beats him, where has the goddess in the post-thread fled? Tell me. Having worshipped properly at the time of marriage the Chandala goddess, who is subject to her devotees,
and served her with her best devotees in a winnowing basket on the bank, living in your own house — when you are bound by Yama's messengers and beaten by the mighty on Yama's road,
where has the hearth-goddess fled, dull-minded fool? Worship Vishnu's feet. When your son is afflicted by fever and the like, having worshipped the Brahma-deva dwelling in the house properly
with incense, lamps, foods and flowers, while living in the house — when you are bound by Yama's messengers and beaten with bamboo nooses and the like,
where has that Brahma-deva fled, dull-minded fool? Worship Vishnu's feet. Having worshipped the brihati plant for offspring and tied the brihati and its fruit to your neck,
when you stand there, bound by Yama's messengers and beaten with brihati thorns, where then has the goddess Brihati fled, dull-minded one? Tell me.
Worship, fool, the supreme deity, Narayana, who carries one across all sorrow; do not set your mind on petty gods, nor listen to empty words.
Putting the petty gods on a javelin and sending them far away, great soul, keep up the dharma of your own family custom, which otherwise becomes a cause of falling into hell.
Purify your body always, dull-minded one, with the eight-syllable mantra at your holy birth-tirtha; giving up the demonic marks in your heart, adorn yourself with Vishnu's excellent marks.
Always, fool, turn to talk of Hari; your life has passed in vain through bad understanding. The company of good Vaishnavas is rare, and the disturbed knowledge whose nature is gradation.
Following Hari and the teacher truly, know your own goal by that, fool. Burning the wicked intellect thus, fool, always worship the one of good understanding.
With me, reaching a true teacher and knowing the principles well with detachment, by that alone we attain liberation, not by crooked ways, through the grace of Vishnu and Lakshmi.'"
Holding this intention in mind, my best devotee spoke thus; so the devotee received the name Pravaha, O lord of birds; now hear the matter at hand.

Taking the cotton given by him, when you stand there and are struck well by Yama's messengers with sharp-edged axes, where has the potter's god with fine fangs and eyes fled, abandoning you? No one knows, even by searching.
The birth of one who never touches a cow, does not know how to milk a cow, and does not care for cows is called meaningless.
For one who does not give a mouthful to a cow or nourish cows there is no goal, none at all; he is held to be like a village outcaste.
While a calf is suckling one should remember the child Krishna; while churning curd one should remember Hari, the support of the churning rod.
At the time of bathing with earth one should remember Hari as Varaha; when applying the upright marks, Keshava and the rest, the twelve.
When wearing the seals one should remember the bearer of conch, discus and mace, the lotus, the Narayana seal, and Kruddholka and the rest.
At the twilight rite, best of birds, one should remember Shri Rama; at the time of shraddha one should remember Achyuta, Ananta and Govinda.
In the five oblations to the breaths one should remember Aniruddha and the others; at the time of offering food one should remember Vasudeva.
At the time of sipping water before eating, Hari within Vayu; at the time of putting on clothes one should remember Hari as Upendra.
When putting on the sacred thread one should remember Narayana called Vamana; and at the time of the arati one should properly remember Vishnu called Parashurama.
